entities.name: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Alcácer Quibir took place on August 14, 1578, at Ksar el-Kebir, Morocco, between the Portuguese and a combined force of the Saadi and Abdali dynasties. This pivotal event marked the end of Portuguese rule in Morocco and the beginning of a period of decline for the Portuguese Empire. The battle was a significant turning point in the history of the region, with far-reaching consequences for the politics and trade of the Western Sahara and the entire Maghreb.

The battle was sparked by the Portuguese attempt to restore their control over the Moroccan coast, which had been largely lost to the Saadi dynasty in the 1550s. The combined forces of the Saadi and Abdali dynasties, led by Abdallah al-Ghalib and Abu Marwan Abd al-Malik, decisively defeated the Portuguese, led by King Sebastian of Portugal. The Portuguese suffered heavy losses, with estimates suggesting that over 70% of their army was killed or captured.

The aftermath of the battle saw the Saadi and Abdali dynasties establish their dominance over Morocco and the surrounding regions. The Portuguese never fully recovered from their losses, and their influence in the region continued to decline. The battle also had significant cultural and economic repercussions, as the Saadi and Abdali dynasties promoted Islamic learning and trade, leading to a flourishing of arts and architecture in the region.

The legacy of the Battle of Alcácer Quibir can be seen in the continued conflict between Morocco and Portugal over the Western Sahara. The battle also marked the beginning of a period of Moroccan dominance in the region, which lasted for centuries and had a profound impact on the politics and culture of the Maghreb.

As historian Ibn Abi Zar wrote, 'The Battle of Alcácer Quibir was a victory for the faith, a triumph of the righteous over the infidels.'
